cards.text: Moses is still preaching to Israel before they go into the land the LORD their God is giving them. Now he's talking about keeping things fair once they live there. Every town, for every tribe, gets judges and officials.

cards.question: Judges and officials in every town. How does Moses say they're to judge the people?

cards.text: Then Moses gives those judges their rules: don't deny justice, don't show partiality and don't accept a bribe. No favorites, friend. Not even for the guy who says your hat looks GREAT.

cards.question: Moses says a bribe even gets to the wise and the righteous. What does it do to them?

answers.text: Blinds their eyes and twists their words
Makes them rich and then makes them lazy
Turns their whole town against them

cards.text: Not just shady folks. The WISE, friend. Slide me a box of chocolate chip cookies before I judge a baking contest, and I can't see ANYBODY else's batch.

cards.question: Moses says to pursue justice, and justice alone, so that you may live and possess the ___ the LORD your God is giving you.

cards.text: Then Moses turns to worship. Don't set up a wooden Asherah pole next to the LORD's altar, and don't set up a sacred pillar for yourselves.

cards.question: Moses says a sacred pillar is something the LORD your God ___.
Next up, sacrifices. True or false: Moses says an ox or a sheep with a serious flaw is fine to offer to the LORD.

cards.text: Moses says that's detestable to the LORD. That's like me handing a baker the cookie I dropped on the floor and calling it a GIFT.
Now a serious case. A man or woman in one of Israel's towns breaks the LORD's covenant and worships other gods, even bowing down to the sun or moon.

cards.question: Somebody reports that a person in town is worshiping other gods. What does Moses say to do first?

answers.text: Send them out of the land

cards.question: True or false: If the report checks out, Moses says the person can go free with a warning.
A death sentence by stoning at the town gates can't rest on just anyone's word. How many witnesses does Moses require?

cards.text: Never on the word of a lone witness. If one coworker says you took his stapler, that's a rumor, but if three say it, friend, we've got a CASE.

cards.question: When the sentence is carried out, the hands of the ___ go first, and after that, the hands of all the people.

cards.text: Witnesses first, then everybody. Moses says you must purge the evil from among you.
Some cases will be too difficult for the town: bloodshed, lawsuits, assaults. The kind where the judge stares at the ceiling for an hour and then asks to phone a friend.

cards.question: When a case is too difficult to judge in town, where does Moses say to take it?

answers.text: The place the LORD will choose
The elders of their own tribe

cards.question: There, they go to the Levitical ___ and to the judge who presides at that time.

cards.text: They inquire, and those leaders give a verdict. Moses says to be careful to do everything they instruct.

cards.question: True or false: Moses says people can adjust the verdict a little if they disagree with it.

cards.text: Moses says, "Do not turn aside to the right or to the left from the decision they declare to you." Basically my phone's GPS: drift one lane over and I hear RECALCULATING.

cards.question: What about a man who acts presumptuously and refuses to listen to the priest or the judge?

answers.text: He must be put to death
He pays a fine to the priests
He is sent out of the town

cards.question: True or false: Moses says when all the people hear about it, they'll be afraid and stop behaving arrogantly.

cards.text: Now Moses looks ahead to a day when Israel is settled in the land and says, let's have a king like all the nations around us. Everybody's got one, so we need one? That's exactly how I ended up with a phone that folds in half.

cards.question: If Israel sets a king over itself, who does Moses say chooses him?
True or false: Moses says Israel may set a foreigner over them as king as long as he's a strong leader.

cards.text: Then Moses lists what the king must not pile up, starting with horses. He's not to get many horses or send the people back to Egypt for more.

cards.question: Why can't the king send the people back to Egypt for horses?

answers.text: The LORD said never go back that way
Pharaoh won't sell horses to Israel
The road there is far too dangerous

cards.question: Moses says the king must not take many wives for himself, or his ___ could go astray.
True or false: Moses says the king may pile up large amounts of silver and gold for himself.

cards.text: Horses, silver, gold: the king's supposed to keep it modest. If that rule covered sprinkles, friend, I'd be off the throne by TUESDAY.
Here's my favorite part. Once he's seated on his royal throne, the king must write for himself a copy of this instruction on a scroll, with the Levitical priests right there.

cards.question: The king's scroll stays with him. How long is he supposed to keep reading from it?

answers.text: All the days of his life

cards.question: Reading it and carefully keeping it helps the king learn to ___ the LORD his God.
True or false: Moses says this keeps the king's heart from being exalted above his countrymen.
What does Moses say comes to a king who keeps this instruction?

answers.text: He and his sons reign many years
He never loses a single battle

cards.text: And he won't turn aside to the right or to the left. That line again, friend, and Moses isn't done preaching yet.

findings.problem: Deuteronomy 16:19 speaks to 'you' (Israel) and never says the commands are given to the judges. 'Then Moses gives those judges their rules' settles who is being spoken to, which the text leaves open.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: This story card has three sentences, and it is not the opening card.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The card only reacts to card 4's answer about the wise. It tells nothing new from the passage and doesn't move forward. It also has three sentences.

rule.text:
Every story card moves the baker forward through the passage.
- No recap cards.

findings.problem: Card 1 already says 'the land the LORD their God is giving them,' which gives away the blank 'land' in the matching phrase from 16:20.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: Deuteronomy 17:2 is conditional ('If a man or woman among you... is found doing evil'). The card drops the 'if' and tells it as something that happens ('A man or woman... breaks the LORD's covenant').
Card 4 says 'Moses says to be careful to do everything they instruct,' which gives away that the verdict can't be adjusted. That makes the true or false answer obvious.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: Card 4 says 'Moses lists what the king must not pile up,' so the baker already knows that piling up silver and gold is not allowed.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The card recaps horses, silver and gold from cards 4 to 7 and adds nothing new. It also uses 'keep it modest,' which isn't in the text, and leaves out the wives.
